cells.tense: The person is turning something over, and their hands are quiet on it now, not rushing.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: There's something you keep weighing. Pick the version that's fair to all of it, your part included, and do that today, without laying out the reasons afterward.
cells.core:
Bearing what must be borne, you stay present while you bear it. Not hardness — the steady kind of strength, the one that keeps your judgment clear under things that would make someone else hurry. Because you don't flinch past the feeling, the fair call shows itself: what's owed both ways, what's right to let go and what's right to keep. The load goes down by deciding, not by being carried another week.

Something in your life is held level while the living part waits on you. Settle it this week, all of it, your share included, and move on it before the day is out. The reasons don't need a hearing. Once the call is made the ground under it goes quiet, and what was propped up gets to grow — which is what you were propping it for.
cells.sheetLine: You can bear the weight and think clearly at once.
cells.verb: releasing what has finished so the living thing can be watered again
cells.place: where the weight is borne steady in the body, and nothing is spent deciding what to do with it

cells.tense: The holding-together is kept ahead of the calendar, so endings don't get their hour.
cells.act: be present to their feeling without drowning in it
cells.ask: Next time someone close is upset, sit with them through it — no fixing, no redirecting, no feeling it for them. Stay until nothing is left unfinished.
cells.core:
Where you bear what many lean on, the bearing has gotten used to arriving first. You spot the next hard thing before it lands and have the shape ready, so nothing concludes without you. What was strength is a pre-emptive grip now, and the endings it holds off are the ground that would let the next real thing grow. Whoever meets you gets the solution, not the feeling.

Sitting near someone while they're upset isn't a load to take on. Stay alongside what they feel and don't step in front of it. That's the smaller version — no plan, no repair, no taking it on. What gets released when you step back comes back as room, for them and for you, and the room is where they finish.

cells.tense: The hand that used to reach for something worth having has stopped moving.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Pick something you'd like to happen, and spend the first fifteen minutes of it today. Fifteen, then leave it until tomorrow.
cells.core:
Where you bear what others lean on, the appetite is what went quiet first. You keep going, you keep being useful, but you've stopped moving toward things — you know how heavy they land when they fall short. Not weakness; a person meeting a demand that doesn't let up, and the reaching went before the going did. What's carried doesn't get lighter while there's no reason for it left in sight.

Wanting something small and doing its first quarter hour puts a little fuel back into wanting itself. Not the whole project, not for anyone else's sake. Direction comes back through moving from what you feel; you don't need to name the feeling before you move first. Done is enough for one day, and the next day you'll have somewhere to start from.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped moving toward things before you stopped going.

cells.tense: The hands are moving on a plan whose author the person would not claim.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: This week, when something lands that you won't take on, name it plainly to whoever asks — then hold the line without explaining why.
cells.core:
Right now you're decisive in a place you wouldn't say you were leading. Calls get made, the hold stays where you put it, the unreasonable thing gets removed by you — and you file it under circumstance. You may well be the one whose week has a shape others move inside, and that shape has an author. Yours. Order serving what it organizes, rather than the reverse, is what this is when the author is known.

Name the thing you won't carry next week, in one sentence. Then leave the sentence where you put it — no explaining, no softening, no doing it anyway. Inside a day or two you'll watch the shape hold, and you'll be standing in it as the one who placed it there.
cells.sheetLine: The calls are yours, filed under circumstance.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is 'the people who depend on you feel the floor hold' — I am assuming there is someone depending on the person, and the record says nothing about dependents. A reader could rightly say nobody leans on them, or that what they carry is not carried for anyone else. If that read is wrong, the asks still survive: deciding a held thing and acting on the same day, treating what is tended as what it now is, letting a want move an hour, and claiming one decision are all useful regardless of who is watching. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'people can stand on it and never notice' — it flatters the holding as a gift to others before the person has said who it is for.

A reader could say they are the one being carried by someone else's structure, not the one making calls. If that read is wrong, the asks survive: deciding a held thing fairly, staying with someone's feeling without fixing it, doing the first fifteen minutes of something wanted, and holding a boundary once are all useful whether or not the person is the one steering. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the week rests on you' — it flatters the bearing as load-bearing for others before the person has said who they bear it for.
